# C-RV26d | Studio generated help, page manifest and scope of shared edits

**Date:** 2 November 2026. Continued from [C-RV26c](PUBLISHER_SUPPORT_CONTENT_AUDIT_C-RV26c_2026-11-02.md). Bounded content-only source audit of author-facing text generated by Website Studio's JavaScript modules, checked against the actual page manifest and publicly authored page files. Preserved previous C-ED/C-RV corrections and the user's established preference for precise, gentle, naturally connected writing.

## Coverage and initial discrepancy

The current `studio/pages.json` contains **15**, not 16, distinct HTML entries. Its groups have **7 Main**, **2 Research**, **2 Projects**, and **4 Teaching resources** pages. **Eleven are locked** against Studio-managed page deletion and **four are not locked**. All 15 entries are unique. The previous C-ED1 ledger's description of a “16-entry” manifest was an **outdated/inaccurate source count**, and later C-RV26a repeated it. The actual manifest content is the authority. Neither earlier report is silently rewritten here; this current dated audit explicitly corrects the count.

All 19 root HTML files previously registered in the comprehensive audit exist, but the 15-entry Studio manifest omits **`pungmul.html`**, **`writing-biological-classification.html`**, the legacy **`about.html`** redirect and **`404.html`**. Pungmul and the independent biological-classification essay are part of the ordinary 16-entry sitemap and remain public academic content, not just old utility files. Studio includes `teaching-osmosis-practice.html`, a separately noindex teaching resource, which is one reason the counts cannot be equated. This inventory describes what Studio exposes, **not an instruction to enlarge the manifest**.

The shared `site-theme.css` is referenced by both listed and unlisted public pages, so theme changes can legitimately be described as site-wide. **Navigation** and **shared header/footer** changes follow different code paths. In `studio/studio-plus.js`, `beforePublish()` iterates `usablePages()` obtained from `state.manifest.pages` and adds `404.html`. In `studio/studio-chrome.js`, its publication hook likewise operates on the manifest's HTML paths plus `404.html`. The two unlisted public pages are **not** touched by either source-based batch for navigation/header/footer. After such a change, unlisted pages **could retain older menus or footers**, creating a cross-page inconsistency. This is a real implementation boundary, not proof that it has occurred in the deployed website.

## User-facing accuracy corrections committed

1. **`studio/index.html`**, commit [89447ff](https://github.com/gmoon-code/gmoon-code.github.io/commit/89447ff338ea24963ef8197b01a7b75362f9184a). The menu help now specifies that it manages **Studio-listed pages**, warns that outside pages may retain their earlier menus until changed separately, and preserves the correct statement that hiding a menu item does not delete the page or its address. This avoids the former suggestion that a menu edit automatically covers *every page on the website*.
2. **`studio/studio-plus.js`**, commit [a9f24ab](https://github.com/gmoon-code/gmoon-code.github.io/commit/a9f24abf94771388d355b066e21dfdc4ba96e1e0). The visible save-status tooltip now says menu changes will update **Studio-listed pages**, not “all pages.” Its adjacent source comment was aligned to the real batch, which also includes `404.html`; JavaScript behavior and page selection remain unchanged.
3. **`studio/studio-chrome.js`**, commit [68f9ac4](https://github.com/gmoon-code/gmoon-code.github.io/commit/68f9ac4f3ee98d3953067cb12c0a2c28bc5d763a). The Header & footer tooltip and post-apply message now scope their claims to **Studio-listed pages** rather than “every page” or the whole website. Source logic remains unchanged and still includes `404.html` in the publication loop.

These revisions name the actual reach of editor actions without disguising an implementation boundary or inventing a feature. The terms “Studio-listed pages” refer to the user-visible page list, not an external service, and are used only where necessary to avoid false coverage claims. The author's public academic paragraphs remain untouched.

## Other checked module text and limits

- `studio/studio-plus.js` defines 22 authoring layouts/blocks with plain descriptions, including section-level prose/image layouts, FAQ, timeline, editable table and process-diagram blocks. Instructions distinguish local drafts and browser recovery from GitHub publication. The draft recovery implementation uses IndexedDB and the source states that token credentials are not stored there.
- `studio/studio-details.js` ties the documented reset control to fine-detail CSS on the selected scope or responsive screen, consistent with C-RV26b. Its contrast hint describes a computed ratio and flags values below 4.5, which is a suitable text-readability cue in the current context, although an actual display/contrast audit was not undertaken.
- `studio/studio-canvas.js` supplies contextual selection, grouping, appearance copy/paste and responsive size controls. Its commands are supported at source-operation level; the successful execution of grouping, drag or resize in a physical browser is **not** inferred from the presence of code.
- `studio/studio-layers.js` provides an explicit “Hide item without deleting it” visibility control and tree-selection status. No wording contradiction was established in the selected code.
- `studio/studio-chrome.js` provides the shared site brand, footer contact text and link labels. Its default email address and other personal contact values remain **unverified user preferences**, not grounds for changing public contact information from a source audit.

## Source verification

**25/25 targeted assertions passed** on re-fetched current sources. These checked actual manifest counts and groups; current files for the two omitted public pages; sitemap presence; both independent `manifest.pages` batch loops and their deliberate `404.html` addition; the shared theme CSS relationship; corrected HTML and dynamic tooltip strings; absence of formerly overbroad strings; earlier fine-detail reset, page-list loading, layer-hide and canvas-appearance commands. All page/JavaScript updates were committed through SHA-guarded file replacement and no source code functionality, manifest page assignments, or research article body was changed.

**Files updated:** `studio/index.html`, `studio/studio-plus.js` and `studio/studio-chrome.js` (exact commits above). Source-only checks do **not** establish live publication parity, external token authorization, the run-time correctness of responsive editing, or repair of the six Editor V2 browser regression failures. A current deployed header/menu consistency inspection is still needed if the owner changes shared site navigation.
